It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} of {{ill|Izumi Province|Q1047117|qid=Q1047117}}. It is also called '''Ishizu Taisha''' and styles itself as “the oldest Ebisu shrine in Japan.” The {{ill|Ebisu (mythology)|Q1129330|qid=Q1129330}} deity is generally said to be hard of hearing, and at Ishizu Shrine a board is set up beside the main hall which worshippers strike with a wooden mallet while voicing their wishes. During the season of the Great Purification (Ōharae), a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=chinowa}} (reed ring) is installed. {{nihongo|'''Ishizu Shrine'''|石津神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Izumi Province]].

== History ==
According to shrine tradition, {{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|lt=Kotoshironushi|Q8009611|qid=Q8009611|lt=Yae Kotoshironushi-no-Kami}} descended to this place carrying five-colored stones, from which the place-name Ishizu is said to have originated. The shrine is identified with the Shikinaisha Ishizu Ōjinja (Iwatsu no Ōjinja), said to have been founded by imperial prayer on August 10 in the 7th year of {{ill|Emperor Kōshō|ar|الإمبراطور كوشو|arz|الامبراطور كوشو|azb|کوشو (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Kōshō|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کۆشۆ|cs|Kóšó|de|Kōshō|eo|Koŝo (japana imperiestro)|es|Kōshō Tennō|fa|امپراتور کوشو|fi|Kōshō|fr|Kōshō (empereur)|he|קושו, קיסר יפן|hr|Kōshō|id|Kaisar Kōshō|it|Kōshō|ja|孝昭天皇|ka|კოსიო|ko|고쇼 천황|lt|Imperatorius Košio|ms|Maharaja Kōshō|nl|Kosho|pl|Kōshō|pt|Kosho (imperador)|ru|Император Косё|sh|Car Kōshō|simple|Emperor Kōshō|sl|Cesar Košo|sr|Кошо (јапански цар)|sv|Kõshõ|th|จักรพรรดิโคโช|tl|Emperador Kosho|tr|Kōshō (imparator)|uk|Імператор Косьо|uz|Imperator Kōshō|vi|Thiên hoàng Kōshō|zh|孝昭天皇|zh_min_nan|Kôsyô Thian-hông|zh_yue|孝昭天皇|qid=Q312841}}. Regarding Ishizu Ōjinja, {{ill|Iwatsuta Shrine|Q11586779|qid=Q11586779}} (Iwatsuta Jinja) in Hamadera Ishizu-chō Naka, {{ill|Nishi-ku, Sakai|Q1042499|qid=Q1042499|lt=Nishi Ward}}, is also considered a candidate shrine; it is thought that originally one was the main shrine and the other a {{ill|Otabisho|Q11489117|qid=Q11489117}} or a branch shrine. Both shrines claim to be “the oldest Ebisu shrine in Japan” as the place where Yae Kotoshironushi-no-Kami (Ebisu deity) descended.

The stones carried by Yae Kotoshironushi-no-Kami are said to be buried in front of the shrine, and are believed to rise up out of the ground in times of natural calamities. In addition, the otabisho where Hiruko-no-Mikoto is said to have washed ashore is located on former coastal land on the north bank of the {{ill|Ishizu River|Q11586780|qid=Q11586780}}.

It is said that during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}}, {{ill|Nomi no Sukune|Q965742|qid=Q965742}}, a descendant of {{ill|Ame no Hohi|lt=Ame-no-Hohi|Q10940685|qid=Q10940685|qid=Q10940685|lt=Ame-no-Hohi-no-Kami}}, became the shrine’s priest.

From {{ill|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|ar|توكوغاوا تسونايوشي|ca|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|cs|Cunajoši Tokugawa|de|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|es|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|eu|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|fa|توکوگاوا تسونایوشی|fi|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|fr|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|id|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|it|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|ja|徳川綱吉|ko|도쿠가와 쓰나요시|mr|तोकुगावा त्सुनायोशी|ms|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|no|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|pl|Tsunayoshi Tokugawa|pt|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|ro|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|ru|Токугава Цунаёси|sk|Cunajoši Tokugawa|sr|Токугава Цунајоши|sv|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|th|โทกูงาวะ สึนาโยชิ|tr|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|uk|Токуґава Цунайосі|vi|Tokugawa Tsunayoshi|zh|德川綱吉|zh_min_nan|Tokugawa Tunayosi|zh_yue|德川綱吉|qid=Q313745}}, {{ill|Shogun|Q131767|qid=Q131767}} of the {{ill|Tokugawa shogunate|Q205662|qid=Q205662}}, the shrine received a shuin land grant in {{ill|Genroku|Q1325001|qid=Q1325001}} 10 ({{ill|1697|Q7702|qid=Q7702}}), and it is said that all of four districts of {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150|lt=Kawachi}} and the vicinity of Sakai were designated as the shrine’s parishioners.

== Access ==
* Bus ({{ill|Nankai Bus|ja|南海バス|qid=Q11408154}})
** From {{ill|Sakaihigashi Station|arz|محطة ساكايهيجاشى|eo|Stacio Sakaihigashi|fr|Gare de Sakaihigashi|it|Stazione di Sakai-Higashi|ja|堺東駅|ko|사카이히가시역|ur|ساکائی ہیگاشی اسٹیشن|zh|堺東站|qid=Q7402783}}, take the bus bound for {{ill|Ōtori|ja|鳳|qid=Q23996403}} Nishimachi-minami and get off at Ishizu Shrine-mae.
* Railway
** {{ill|Hankai Line|Q5648522|qid=Q5648522|lt=Hankai Line}}: 7-minute walk from {{ill|Ishizu Station|eo|Stacio Ishizu (Osaka)|ja|石津停留場|ko|이시즈 정류장|zh|石津停留場|qid=Q11586796}}
** {{ill|Nankai Main Line|Q59453|qid=Q59453}}: 10-minute walk from {{ill|Ishizugawa Station|arz|محطة ايشيزوجاوا|it|Stazione di Ishizugawa|ja|石津川駅|ko|이시즈가와역|my|အိရှိဇုဂဝဘူတာ|ur|ایشیزوگاوا اسٹیشن|zh|石津川站|qid=Q6080457}}
